question: Compare the top three open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products.
aliases: Compare the top 3 open source vector databases for a startup building RAG products
Which open-source vector database should a RAG startup use?

plan.objective: Compare three widely used open-source vector databases for a startup building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) products.
plan.interpretation: Compare Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate on licensing and self-hosting, hybrid search and filtering, operational complexity, and independent performance evidence, from the point of view of a small team building RAG products.
assumptions: "Top" is read as widely used, actively maintained, open source, and self-hostable. The three databases are compared, not ranked.
The startup is a small team that may self-host before moving to a managed service.

documents.title: Qdrant documentation: overview
documents.snippet: Qdrant is an open-source vector database and similarity search engine written in Rust, licensed under Apache 2.0.
documents.content:
Qdrant overview

Qdrant is an open-source vector database and similarity search engine written in Rust. It is distributed under the Apache License 2.0 and can be self-hosted with Docker or Kubernetes, or used through a managed cloud service.

Qdrant supports hybrid search by combining dense vectors with sparse vectors in a single query. Payload filters can be applied during the vector search rather than only after it.

In distributed mode, Qdrant splits collections into shards and replicates them across nodes, using the Raft consensus protocol for cluster metadata. Our published benchmarks show Qdrant delivering high throughput on the datasets we tested.

documents.title: Milvus documentation: architecture overview
documents.snippet: Milvus is an open-source vector database released under Apache 2.0 and a graduated project of the LF AI & Data Foundation.
documents.content:
Milvus architecture overview

Milvus is an open-source vector database released under the Apache License 2.0. It is a graduated project of the LF AI & Data Foundation.

Milvus supports hybrid search across multiple vector fields, including sparse vectors for keyword-style matching, and scalar filtering on entity fields.

Milvus can run as Milvus Lite inside a Python process, as a single-node standalone server, or as a distributed cluster. A distributed deployment depends on additional components, including etcd for metadata, object storage, and a message queue. Milvus is built to scale to billions of vectors.

documents.title: Weaviate documentation: introduction
documents.snippet: Weaviate is an open-source vector database written in Go and released under the BSD 3-Clause license.
documents.content:
Introduction to Weaviate

Weaviate is an open-source vector database written in Go and released under the BSD 3-Clause license. Teams can self-host it with Docker or Kubernetes or use a managed service.

Weaviate's hybrid search combines keyword search using BM25 with vector search and merges the two result sets with a configurable weighting.

Weaviate scales horizontally by sharding collections across nodes, and replication can be configured per collection for availability. Weaviate is used in production by companies building search and retrieval-augmented generation applications.

documents.title: Self-hosting Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate: notes from a small team
documents.snippet: We ran Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate on our own infrastructure for a retrieval-augmented generation prototype.
documents.content:
Self-hosting three vector databases

We ran Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate on our own infrastructure for a retrieval-augmented generation prototype. All three were straightforward to start on a single machine with Docker.

The biggest operational difference appeared when we moved to a cluster. Milvus in distributed mode required us to operate etcd, object storage, and a message queue alongside the database itself, while Qdrant and Weaviate each ran as a single service type per node.

For a small team, the number of moving parts mattered more to us than raw query speed.

documents.title: Why filtering during vector search matters
documents.snippet: Filtering during the search, rather than after it, avoids returning fewer results than requested.
documents.content:
Filtering during vector search

Many RAG applications restrict retrieval to one tenant, product, or date range. Filtering during the search, rather than after it, avoids returning fewer results than requested when filters are selective.

When comparing databases, test filtered queries with realistic metadata, because unfiltered results can hide this difference.

documents.content:
Top 10 vector databases in 2026

Qdrant is the fastest vector database for every workload, and Milvus is the most popular choice for enterprises. Weaviate is a strong all-rounder with a friendly API.

This list reflects our editors' opinions and is not based on a controlled benchmark.

documents.title: Independent benchmark of open-source vector databases for filtered search
documents.snippet: This report compares Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate on the same hardware using public embedding datasets.
documents.content:
Independent benchmark of open-source vector databases

This report compares Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate on the same hardware using public embedding datasets and a fixed recall target. None of the vendors funded or reviewed the study.

No engine led on every dataset. Results depended heavily on index parameters, filter selectivity, and hardware, so the order changed between test configurations.

We recommend that teams benchmark their own data and filters before choosing.

short_answer.text: Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate are all open source, can be self-hosted, and support hybrid search. The clearest difference is operational: a distributed Milvus deployment depends on etcd, object storage, and a message queue. An independent benchmark found that no engine led on every dataset, so the choice should follow your own data, filters, and team capacity rather than a ranking.

findings.text: For a small team, the number of moving parts in a cluster may matter more than raw query speed when choosing among the three.

overclaim.text: Qdrant is the fastest of the three for every RAG workload.

limitations: The comparison covers three databases chosen as widely used and self-hostable; other options such as pgvector or Elasticsearch were not evaluated.
Performance evidence comes from one independent benchmark whose results depended on configuration.
